thread:
sara: Heads-up — we need a short proposal for the mixed-capacity pool defaults for next week's release. Focus: min on-demand floor formula, burst pool sizing, and interruption handling.

nolan: Quick idea — set a min_on_demand floor based on request p50 latency sensitivity and committed capacity. Something like: `min = max(ceil(0.06 * committed_gpus), 2)` so tiny tenants still have some on-demand.

kevin: I like anchored to committed. Curious about region variance — some regions have higher spot churn. We should bake a regional multiplier (e.g., 1.0 in stable regions, 1.3 in volatile regions).

maya: +1. Also add a hard cap on burst % so we don't oversubscribe spot. Proposal: burst_capacity <= 40% of active pool in default config. Can be overridden per-tenant.

sara: Good. How do we handle interruptions mid-inference? We can't always rely on retries for long streaming requests.

liam: Two things: 1) hedged requests for tail-sensitive flows — send to on-demand and spot in parallel with quick cancel. 2) checkpointing for long-running sessions — persist KV-cache every N tokens to Redis to recover on fallback.

sanjay: For cost-sensitive, hedging doubles calls => cost impact. Suggest heuristics: hedged only for requests > 1s compute or when model size > X. Otherwise prefer rapid fallback routing rather than parallel hedging.

autoscale-bot: Reminder: current autoscaler has a minimum scale delay of 120s. That affects our effective floor during sudden drains.

kevin: Noted. We should tune scale delay per pool type: burst pools shorter (30s) so they can reclaim spot quickly, base on-demand pools keep longer to avoid churn.

maya: Ops playbook: when a spot tranche drains, auto-shift up to on-demand for affected sessions using graceful handoff: mark sessions READONLY -> spawn new on-demand pod -> resume. Add circuit-breaker if on-demand capacity exhausted.

erin: Can we put an inexpensive safety net for multi-tenant noisy neighbors? e.g., tenant-level reserve credits that convert to guaranteed on-demand when their error rate spikes.

sara: Love it. Action items:
- Nolan: draft min_on_demand formula with regional multiplier and example table for committed sizes.
- Maya: propose burst_capacity default and override flow + autoscaler delta times.
- Liam & Sanjay: define hedging thresholds and checkpoint cadence (token interval).
- Kevin: update handoff playbook + circuit-breaker states.
- Erin: sketch tenant reserve credit behavior.

sara: timeline: draft by EOD tomorrow, sync Wed 10am. If anyone wants to pair on wording ping me.

liam: I'll drop a short diagram in the doc — topology of hedged vs fallback routing.

maya: tagging @kevin for the playbook bits :thumbsup:

kevin: 👍 will take playbook. Also adding one-off metric: "eviction-induced-fallbacks" to track how often we hit on-demand because of spot drains.

sanjay: Suggest alert: if eviction-induced-fallbacks > 5% of traffic in 10m -> trigger capacity review and possibly raise min_on_demand.

sara: Perfect. I'll assemble and open the PR once drafts are in. Thanks all.
